rv.q: This is a meticulous and artfully conceived blend of storytelling, technology and actorly skill, running a tight 90 minutes.
If you've come to be scared, you're in the right place. This is a good, old-fashioned ghost-train of a story.

But horror theatre is a small, weird and often terrible genre and this is a proper scary little gem – what with the West End’s Paranormal Activity, we’re living through a mini golden age for scares on stage.
So it is with the first half-hour of A Ghost in Your Ear, which fills the intimate studio space at the Hampstead Theatre with dread even while it holds back on any shocks.
It's expertly atmospheric – a masterclass in staging horror slickly – and fortunately, its trappings are enough to excuse the slightly naff and overly familiar story.
This production too must surely have a life beyond its initial run, which is scheduled to conclude on 31st January.
A Ghost in Your Ear is smart, intricately-crafted, and properly scary – bring a friend to hold onto!
Whether or not you believe in ghosts, this should prove at the very least a decent work out for your adrenal gland.
It’s a very clever spin on an otherwise classic structure: man tells ghost story; man becomes part of ghost story.
Entertaining more than it was eerie, it was a thoughtful and satisfying experience.
The result is an absolutely outstanding production, and the first 5-star show of the year - one that will haunt you long after you leave the theatre.
Eerie and mesmerising, A Ghost in Your Ear feels much longer than a 90-minute thrill in the way in which it completely immerses the listener in the experience.
A Ghost In Your Ear is a good old fashioned story which encourages careful viewing and listening to deliver a very, very satisfying outcome.
A Ghost In Your Ear is a bold, atmospheric piece that redefines how we experience theatre, proving that horror can thrive in the intimacy of sound as much as in the spectacle of sight.
The headphone gimmick might feel unnecessary, taking away rather than adding to the story, but even so A ghost In Your Ear still succeeds in delivering a fun spooky story with a few genuine scares.
The final big scare is telegraphed strongly enough that it works as a cathartic big laugh rather than horror...

cn.t: Critics praise this inventive horror for its atmospheric binaural sound design and effective scares, though some find the ghost story itself overly familiar. Armitage's headphone-based thriller delivers genuine chills despite a predictable narrative.
